meeting.title: Air Fleet Capital - Partner Intro - Google Chrome

content.speaker: Speaker 1
content.text:
Stay in the AC, all right? Hey, Kailash. So, Anne, I know we're still waiting on people, but this is Kailash from the Dataskate team. He's one of our preferred implementation partners, and so this is who you'll be meeting today. We'll just wait for the rest of the crew to join. Sounds good, thank you.
So, Anne, are you a pilot as well?

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: I'm not, no. [Laughter].

content.speaker: Speaker 1
content.text: I feel like most of the team is, right?

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: Well, Jim was at one time, so really only Jim had his license, so everybody else... Some people would like to work towards it, but they don't really have their pilot license yet.

content.speaker: Speaker 1
content.text: Right? Cool. Okay, it looks like we got Daniel on here. Nicole, hey Daniel, good. So Daniel, this is Anne.

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: Nice to meet you. I don't know if you knew the old rad Max Jevnick. I am Max's temporary coverage on the core side, but I worked with Nicole and the integrations team, so just wanted to come on and put a face to the name. I was going to reach out to Jim and Spencer separately, but Nicole plugged in on these conversations, so just wanted to pop in and say hello.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: Nice to meet you.

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: Nice to meet you as well.

content.speaker: Speaker 1
content.text: So we're just waiting on Jim and Spencer.

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text: Okay, how are we doing today, teams? While we're waiting, how's everybody doing?

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: Weekend as usual.

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text: A little too short, yes, maybe I know the feeling. Did you get anything good done over the weekend, though? Anything fun happened?

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: Now, I was telling the whole it's too hot here to do anything, so, in Arizona, it's like you try not to go outside too much.

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text:
I totally get that. Yeah, it was a little too hot in New York as well. I mean, it's not 110 degrees like it is there, but it was in the 90s and really humid. So, yeah, it was just like seeking shade and just running away from that. We have our ten-month-old.
So we had fun, we got some ice cream, but it was like a constant exercise of me holding the umbrella over him to find where the sun is in any given moment, to not let that hit him. But, yes. Other than that, it was good. Definitely an air conditioning inside...

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: Though, right? Yeah. So... In Arizona, do you guys have to get anything done outside by like 8 in the morning, right? Or it's just too late?

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: Yeah, it is, because it's once the... I call it the death rate once it comes up. I think you're just like, "It's just so hot. It's more intense, I think, because it's not so humid here, so there's nothing to block it, so it's just like this intense..."

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: But class, it's a dry heat. Yeah, well, it's still hot because it's still unbearable. I walk out. [Laughter].

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text:
You can go in the shade, though, and you don't sweat. If you're not in the direct sunlight, it's not as bad as it is. I mean, as long as the wind isn't blowing the higher... But if it's just nice and still, it's really not too bad in the shade.
It's not like on the East Coast where you go outside and you're just instantly sweating regardless of where you are.

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: It's not my humidity.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: So it is a little different, but it's still when it's over 110, I'm like, "Okay, that's just too hot."

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: Yeah, I was actually in Scottsdale in March for spring training. So I saw a couple of games and yeah, I'd echo that in the shade. It's fine. Stay out there long enough in the sun, and I'm sure March is nothing compared to July and August.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text:
This March was really warm compared to usual. Usually it's only in like the 70 s or 80 s that time of year. So we kind of got shipped with our winner this year because it was already it hit like a hundred degrees in March, but then it did cool off, which was good, but it still felt like we missed part of our winter.
[Laughter].

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: Dylan, Nicole, I know this is your guys' show. I think we need Jim and then Spencer from the Airfleet side.

content.speaker: Speaker 1
content.text: Yes.

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: Okay.

content.speaker: Speaker 1
content.text: Yeah, we're in on them. Are you in the office with them?

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text:
By any chance? They're not. Jim's traveling, so I'm texting him now to ask him if he's joining the call. Spencer? I think he's out today or he's on vacation, but I thought he said he was going to call in.
I have his number and texted him.

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text:
Nicole, I was paying to you earlier. I don't know if... I don't know if you have the emails for Spencer on this invite. If you look at the GE, it's at least different than what I have listed for him.
But maybe I'm wrong.

content.speaker: Speaker 1
content.text: Yeah, it looks like it's Anne Madrano at VO.

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: It looks like it is a combo. Then I see Spencer Madrano for him. So let me just add... I see... I don't know if I can because it's my call.

content.speaker: Speaker 1
content.text: Which might be why he couldn't call in if this was the wrong email.

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: Yeah. I just added what I see as his email: emajrao@airfleetcapital.com, and I sent a notification with it.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text:
Thank you for...
Yeah, I don't know, I don't want to keep everyone waiting because Jim hasn't responded to the text. I'm not sure.

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text: Yeah, no worries. Do you think it'll be better if we try to reschedule? I know he's traveling, but do you think that if we try to do it the same time tomorrow... Do you think you'd be open to it?

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: I think that might be better since you haven't responded today.

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text: Let's do it while we're here. Is there anything that we can do for you before we part ways?

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: I don't think so. I think it's good.

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text: Okay, right on. Well, why don't we just put it down in the calendar for 9 AM tomorrow? Does that work for all parties on the call? Okay, right now, so let's do that, and then we'll see you tomorrow.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: Okay. All right, thank you. All right, then I'll follow up with good.

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: Nice to meet you, I.
